tools.description: Load url in a tab, or go back, forward or reload, and wait until the page is ready. Reports the final URL and title, failed requests, console errors and Service Worker registrations

read.description: also return the page in this call: markdown (main content), text, html or records (one row per listing card). A failed, timed-out, superseded or off-site navigation returns the failure, not content

read_scope.description: CSS selector scoping the read, as page_read scope

url.description: required for goto, the default action: the address to load, with scheme

wait.description: settled: committed, loaded, no request in flight, 250 ms of network quiet. dom: load, then DOM unchanged for 100 ms, max 3 s; a page that fetches content after load may return as a skeleton. load: load event only. none: return now

wait_for.description: CSS selector that must also be present before returning

tools.name: navigate

tools.description: Run interaction steps on a page in one call. Steps run in order and stop at the first failure unless a step sets continue_on_error. A login is one call: fill #email, click Log in, then wait for url_contains /dashboard. Each step reports what it changed (DOM, URL, dialog), the network requests it triggered and console errors. fill drives React and Vue controlled inputs and select elements

action.description: click, fill, select, check, press, hover, scroll or wait

continue_on_error.description: run later steps even if this one fails

count.description: CSS selectors to count before and after this step, to see whether a click loaded more

gone.description: wait: until target, text or url is ABSENT

predicate.description: wait: JS boolean expression, isolated world

require_visible.description: wait: the selector must be visible, not just present

role.description: ARIA role filter for a text target, such as button or link

settle_ms.description: ms to settle after the step, default 600 for click, else 0

submit.description: fill: press Enter after setting the value

target.description: snapshot ref such as e5, CSS selector or accessible-name text, tried in that order. wait: the CSS selector to wait for

text_contains.description: wait: until page text contains this

url_contains.description: wait: until the URL contains this

value.description: fill, select: the value; a checkbox takes true or false. check: true or false. press: a key such as Enter or Escape. scroll: top, bottom or a pixel offset

watch.description: targets whose visible, enabled and value state to report before and after this step

within.description: only match inside this ref or CSS selector

tools.name: page_act

tools.description: Run JavaScript in a tab and return the value of the last expression; a returned Promise is awaited. isolated world: full DOM access, immune to page CSP, but page JS globals and the expandos page scripts set on DOM nodes (React fiber keys, __vue internals) are invisible; on Firefox read globals via window.wrappedJSObject. main world: the page's own world, which sees everything; a strict page CSP can block it, and the result says so
tools.name: page_eval

tools.description: Read a page's content. markdown extracts the main content with Defuddle, stripping navigation, ads and page chrome and keeping title, site and author; it falls back to plain text if extraction fails

frame_id.description: iframe to read; page_snapshot and an empty read list the ids

max_chars.description: characters per call; continue with offset

offset.description: continue reading from this character offset

scope.description: CSS selector. markdown: treat this subtree as the main content; text, html: read only this subtree

url.description: navigate here first, then read, in one call, same as navigate with read=format; uses tab_id, else the active tab

tools.name: page_read

tools.description: Capture a tab as an inline image with a short text summary. Firefox captures background tabs without taking focus, except a page left with no layout (0x0) by a minimized or background window; Chromium briefly activates the tab. Each shot first waits briefly for web fonts, image decode and a quiet animation frame

selector.description: capture one element by snapshot ref, CSS selector or visible text, cropped to its box; overrides full_page. Zero or several matches is an error

settle_ms.description: cap in ms on the pre-shot wait, default about 1200; 0 skips it

tools.name: page_screenshot

tools.description: Map a page's interactive elements, one line each: ref role "name" value/state selector. Pass a ref such as e5 or the selector as a page_act target. Runs of same-name controls collapse to one line with a count; iframes are listed at the end with their frame_ids. forms mode: radio and checkbox groups with their options and current selection, inputs with values, buttons with enabled state. records mode: one row per repeated card (product grid, search results) with title, link, prices and image, each read from inside that card. A card with more than one live price is AMBIGUOUS and lists the candidates, each with the words beside it; struck-through prices are reported separately; tracking redirects are unwrapped. With no confident pattern it refuses; then pass item_selector

item_selector.description: records only: CSS selector matching one card

root.description: CSS selector of the subtree to map

tools.name: page_snapshot

tools.description: See the headers and bodies a page sends: cookies, auth headers, its own XHRs. Cookie and auth header values come back <redacted>, which still shows they were sent; bodies come back raw by default. recent: the per-tab log of the last ~300 requests (method, URL, status, timing), retroactive, no monitor needed; successful static assets are hidden; no headers or bodies, those need a monitor. start: capture url_patterns such as */api/*; returns a monitor_id that expires after options.ttl_seconds. list: captured request summaries for monitor_id. get: one capture in full; request_id must belong to that monitor. Headers appear ONLY here. stop: end the monitor. get returns request_headers, response_headers, request_body and response_body, each body as {included, content, content_type, encoding, size_bytes, truncated, note}; note says why a body is missing. request_headers == {} never means none were sent; request_headers_note says why they were not captured, usually a cache hit

action.description: recent, start, stop, list or get

filter.description: recent: JS regex over the URL

include_binary.description: get: return binary bodies as base64; capture them by widening options.content_types_to_capture

options.description: start overrides. ttl_seconds: monitor lifetime, default 10 minutes, 10s..1h. max_body_size: bytes per body, default 50000, clamped 1000..1000000; longer bodies are truncated. content_types_to_capture: default JSON and text. sensitive_headers: extra header names to redact; a display filter, not a capture filter. authorization, cookie, set-cookie and similar are always <redacted> and no argument reveals them

request_id.description: get: the captured request, from list

tab_id.description: recent: the tab whose log to read, default active tab. start: capture only this tab, default all tabs

url_patterns.description: start, required: glob URL patterns to capture

tools.name: requests

tools.description: Is BrowserPlug working? Reports the connected browsers, which one this session drives, the MCP clients on the shared server, the request-queue depth and limit, and any failed precondition with its remedy. Call it first when page tools get no response. For file:// tabs, extension_file_access.can_read_opened_file_tab says whether page_* tools can read one the user has open (a per-user toggle); can_open_file_url says whether BrowserPlug can open one: never on Firefox, on Chromium once that toggle is on

verbose.description: add the full connection dump; large, and the summary has everything diagnostic

tools.description:
Pick which of the 2 connected browsers your calls drive. Each is a separate logged-in profile, and tabs, navigate, page_* and requests act in one of them: until you switch, the server default marked below (the pinned browser, else the first to connect). The choice is per-MCP-client and sticky; it moves only your session. Tab ids and page_snapshot refs do not carry across browsers. If the browser you chose disconnects, calls fail instead of falling back

  [1] firefox-dev; Firefox Developer Edition 150.0   <- server default
  [2] chrome; Chrome 150.0

action.description: click, fill, select, check, press, hover, scroll or wait

continue_on_error.description: run later steps even if this one fails

count.description: CSS selectors to count before and after this step, to see whether a click loaded more

gone.description: wait: until target, text or url is ABSENT

predicate.description: wait: JS boolean expression, isolated world

require_visible.description: wait: the selector must be visible, not just present

role.description: ARIA role filter for a text target, such as button or link

settle_ms.description: ms to settle after the step, default 600 for click, else 0

submit.description: fill: press Enter after setting the value

target.description: snapshot ref such as e5, CSS selector or accessible-name text, tried in that order. wait: the CSS selector to wait for

text_contains.description: wait: until page text contains this

url_contains.description: wait: until the URL contains this

value.description: fill, select: the value; a checkbox takes true or false. check: true or false. press: a key such as Enter or Escape. scroll: top, bottom or a pixel offset

watch.description: targets whose visible, enabled and value state to report before and after this step

within.description: only match inside this ref or CSS selector

tools.name: page_act

tools.description: Run JavaScript in a tab and return the value of the last expression; a returned Promise is awaited. isolated world: full DOM access, immune to page CSP, but page JS globals and the expandos page scripts set on DOM nodes (React fiber keys, __vue internals) are invisible; on Firefox read globals via window.wrappedJSObject. main world: the page's own world, which sees everything; a strict page CSP can block it, and the result says so
tools.name: page_eval

tools.description: Read a page's content. markdown extracts the main content with Defuddle, stripping navigation, ads and page chrome and keeping title, site and author; it falls back to plain text if extraction fails

frame_id.description: iframe to read; page_snapshot and an empty read list the ids

max_chars.description: characters per call; continue with offset

offset.description: continue reading from this character offset

scope.description: CSS selector. markdown: treat this subtree as the main content; text, html: read only this subtree

url.description: navigate here first, then read, in one call, same as navigate with read=format; uses tab_id, else the active tab

tools.name: page_read

tools.description: Capture a tab as an inline image with a short text summary. Firefox captures background tabs without taking focus, except a page left with no layout (0x0) by a minimized or background window; Chromium briefly activates the tab. Each shot first waits briefly for web fonts, image decode and a quiet animation frame

selector.description: capture one element by snapshot ref, CSS selector or visible text, cropped to its box; overrides full_page. Zero or several matches is an error

settle_ms.description: cap in ms on the pre-shot wait, default about 1200; 0 skips it

tools.name: page_screenshot

tools.description: Map a page's interactive elements, one line each: ref role "name" value/state selector. Pass a ref such as e5 or the selector as a page_act target. Runs of same-name controls collapse to one line with a count; iframes are listed at the end with their frame_ids. forms mode: radio and checkbox groups with their options and current selection, inputs with values, buttons with enabled state. records mode: one row per repeated card (product grid, search results) with title, link, prices and image, each read from inside that card. A card with more than one live price is AMBIGUOUS and lists the candidates, each with the words beside it; struck-through prices are reported separately; tracking redirects are unwrapped. With no confident pattern it refuses; then pass item_selector

item_selector.description: records only: CSS selector matching one card

root.description: CSS selector of the subtree to map

tools.name: page_snapshot

tools.description: See the headers and bodies a page sends: cookies, auth headers, its own XHRs. Cookie and auth header values come back <redacted>, which still shows they were sent; bodies come back raw by default. recent: the per-tab log of the last ~300 requests (method, URL, status, timing), retroactive, no monitor needed; successful static assets are hidden; no headers or bodies, those need a monitor. start: capture url_patterns such as */api/*; returns a monitor_id that expires after options.ttl_seconds. list: captured request summaries for monitor_id. get: one capture in full; request_id must belong to that monitor. Headers appear ONLY here. stop: end the monitor. get returns request_headers, response_headers, request_body and response_body, each body as {included, content, content_type, encoding, size_bytes, truncated, note}; note says why a body is missing. request_headers == {} never means none were sent; request_headers_note says why they were not captured, usually a cache hit

action.description: recent, start, stop, list or get

filter.description: recent: JS regex over the URL

include_binary.description: get: return binary bodies as base64; capture them by widening options.content_types_to_capture

options.description: start overrides. ttl_seconds: monitor lifetime, default 10 minutes, 10s..1h. max_body_size: bytes per body, default 50000, clamped 1000..1000000; longer bodies are truncated. content_types_to_capture: default JSON and text. sensitive_headers: extra header names to redact; a display filter, not a capture filter. authorization, cookie, set-cookie and similar are always <redacted> and no argument reveals them

request_id.description: get: the captured request, from list

tab_id.description: recent: the tab whose log to read, default active tab. start: capture only this tab, default all tabs

url_patterns.description: start, required: glob URL patterns to capture

tools.name: requests

tools.description: Is BrowserPlug working? Reports the connected browsers, which one this session drives, the MCP clients on the shared server, the request-queue depth and limit, and any failed precondition with its remedy. Call it first when page tools get no response. For file:// tabs, extension_file_access.can_read_opened_file_tab says whether page_* tools can read one the user has open (a per-user toggle); can_open_file_url says whether BrowserPlug can open one: never on Firefox, on Chromium once that toggle is on

verbose.description: add the full connection dump; large, and the summary has everything diagnostic

tools.name: server_info

tools.description: Open, find, close and switch the user's browser tabs and windows. Open your own tab with tabs(action="open", background=true, url="https://…")

action.description: list: open tabs grouped by window. active: the tab page_* tools use when tab_id is omitted. find: tabs whose URL or title contains url. open: load url in a new tab or window. close: a tab, or a whole window via window_id. activate: bring tab_id to the front. window: move, resize, minimize or maximize a window. routing: report a tab's proxy

background.description: open only. Leave the user on their current tab; page_* tools drive a background tab by its id

focus_window.description: activate and window. true raises the window; false acts without taking focus, but an unfocused or minimized window is not painted and screenshots blank

incognito.description: open only. A private window, without the profile's cookies or logins

new_window.description: open only. A new window instead of a tab, sharing the profile's cookies and logins

pinned.description: open only. Pin the new tab

recent.description: list only. true: the recently used tabs plus a count of the rest; false: every open tab

state.description: window only: normal, minimized, maximized or fullscreen

tab_id.description: tab id from list, find or active, for activate, close and routing; routing defaults to the active tab

url.description: required for open and find. open: the address to load, with scheme. find: a case-insensitive literal substring of a tab's URL or title; one distinctive word beats a phrase

width.description: pixels: the new width for window, or the initial width of a new_window or incognito window; ignored when maximized or fullscreen

window_id.description: window id from list. close: the whole window instead of one tab. window: the window to change, default the focused one. open: the window for the new tab

tools.name: tabs
